customManagers.description: Widen gemspec upper bounds (`'< N'`) to the major after the newest release, e.g. `'>= 2.0.0', '< 3.0'` -> `'>= 2.0.0', '< 4'`. The current value is the bound as a Ruby prerelease (`3.0.a`), which sorts above every release the bound allows and below `3.0.0`, so any release at or past the bound is an update. The built-in gemspec manager can't do this: its strategies derive the new bound from the old one (`< 3.0` -> `< 3.1.3`, `< 11` -> `< 13.4.3`)
Update Ruby versions in GitHub Actions matrix entries (which the github-actions manager doesn't see), marked with a `# renovate: datasource=ruby-version depName=ruby` comment

packageRules.description: Applies ":preserveSemverRanges" to the custom manager above. See: https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/discussions/28090

Offer Ruby patch updates separately from minor ones. Otherwise a pinned 3.2.x is only offered the newest non-major Ruby (e.g. 3.4.x), which the next rule disables, so it never gets a 3.2 patch release

Only take patch updates for Ruby itself. CI Ruby versions are pinned per major.minor on purpose (e.g. 3.2 is the Ruby the OpenVox 8 agent ships, 4.0 is OpenVox 9's), so moving to a new minor or major is a deliberate change made by hand
Group Ruby patch updates into one PR per repository
json 3.x breaks OpenVox 8's Puppet::Util::Json (every rspec-puppet compile raises ArgumentError). Hold it below 3 until OpenVox 8 support has been dropped
gemspec dependencies are ranges and stay wide: an outgrown `~> X` becomes `'>= X', '< next major'` instead of moving to `~> Y`, which would drop the older releases
Upper bounds (`< N`) are widened by the gemspec custom manager above, so the built-in gemspec manager doesn't propose its own, narrower bound for them
One update per upper bound, to the newest release, rather than one per major or minor in between
